verdict.rationale: Kit issues per-app delegated credentials through OAuth 2.0, with PKCE, refresh-token, and token-revocation flows, and it offers separate API keys for automating your own account. This lets an agent get its own revocable credentials instead of sharing account logins. However, nothing in the evidence describes OAuth scopes, read-only keys, or per-resource permission limits, and the Kit MCP is described as having full read and write access to the account. Missing for 10: documented granular scopes or permission levels for API keys or OAuth tokens, least-privilege or read-only agent credentials, scope controls on the Kit MCP, and independent corroboration.
